extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners interested in peer review processes (scientometrics scholars, journal editors, and study designers of peer-review systems)
extracted.subtask_description: Coding and evaluating reviewer comments and public (short) comments in a public peer review system to determine which thematic areas commentators focus on and how comments support selection vs. improvement. Uses a nine-area classification scheme and coder ratings of comment usefulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria concerning the future 'gain' that could result from publication of a manuscript — scientiﬁc advancement, importance for journal readers, or practical usefulness; aspects of importance, newness, and originality of the research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'The paper is relevant since it highlights several shortcomings in…'; 'The results are important for the atmospheric science community'; 'This paper adds little to the existing body of literature…'. Used to judge potential contribution and novelty; important for selection decisions (high-impact journals emphasize relevance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing and Presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal qualities of a manuscript: writing style, written expression, spelling, grammar, professional appearance, adherence to submission guidelines, appropriate length, and thoroughness (presence of all necessary information in each section).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'The paper is well written and it appears to be scientiﬁcally sound'; 'The introduction does not show a clear objective of this work'; 'The authors used too many abbreviations…'; 'I would favor a re-writing of this section…'. Includes checks for completeness and readability; high frequency category in ACP comments (largest share of statements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Design and Conception
rubrics_metrics.description: Adequacy and correctness of the conceptual framework and research design: internal consistency, plausibility of design relative to research question, sampling quality, generalizability, and replicability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'This paper is excellent from the point of view of sampling and analytical procedures'; 'The current records are too short'; '…a number of control experiments are required to eliminate the uncertainties…'. Evaluates whether study conception and design support the claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods and Statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Correctness, appropriateness, and (where relevant) novelty of methods and statistical analyses; quality of operationalization of key constructs and data measurement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'It is not demonstrated how well the parameterization works'; '…more sophisticated methods are needed'; '…a more extensive sensitivity and uncertainty analysis must be carried out…'. Focuses on methodological validity and adequacy of analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion of Results
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether conclusions are objective, correct, and properly based on results; clarity/existence of a take-home message; breadth and depth of the discussion section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'The discussion of the results is very appropriate'; 'The conclusions are consistent with the results'; 'The speculation on possible mechanisms … is very vague'; 'The “Results” presented … are not sufﬁcient to validate the method'. Judges interpretive soundness and whether claims overreach data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to the Literature and Documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree to which the manuscript is embedded in the relevant literature: up-to-date literature review, thoroughness of referencing, and appropriate citation/documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Previous work is well reviewed'; 'the authors should refer to this article…'; '…number and quality of references is appropriate…'; 'why are the results of… not included in the discussion?'. Checks completeness and context-setting in citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theory
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the manuscript contributes to theory development and whether the theoretical basis of the research is complete and sound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples (implicit): comments that evaluate contribution to theory or soundness/completeness of theoretical framing. (Area had relatively few assigned coding units in this dataset.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Author’s Reputation and/or Institutional Affiliation
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the manuscript in light of the authors' scholarly reputation or institutional affiliation; comments referencing prior standing or known work of the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Knowing the reliability and merits of the … group … I am optimistic that fully transparent model documentation will be made available…'; 'Building on earlier work … he does a nice job in…'; includes implicit bias-related considerations (rare overall in this dataset).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria concerning compliance with scientific ethics or discipline-specific ethics standards (e.g., plagiarism, duplicate publication, intentional omission of relevant literature).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Half of the results have already been published elsewhere…'; 'The authors intentionally avoid to cite literature showing…'; used to detect ethical problems or misconduct-related concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment helps editors decide (selection usefulness)
rubrics_metrics.description: A coder-rated measure of whether a given comment helps editors decide whether a manuscript should be published (5-point scale: 1 = very helpful to 5 = not helpful at all).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scoring guidance used in study: 1–5 scale; reviewer comments (RCs) tended to score median = 2 (helpful), short comments (SCs) median = 4 (less helpful). Used to evaluate the comment's contribution to the selection function of peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment helps authors improve manuscript (improvement usefulness)
rubrics_metrics.description: A coder-rated measure of whether a given comment helps authors to improve the manuscript (5-point scale: 1 = very helpful to 5 = not helpful at all).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scoring guidance used in study: 1–5 scale; RCs tended to be rated more helpful for improvement than SCs. Used to evaluate the comment's contribution to the improvement/quality-enhancement function of peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extent comment addresses manuscript content
rubrics_metrics.description: A coder-rated measure of the extent to which the comment addresses substantive content of the manuscript (5-point scale: 1 = very clear/addresses content well to 5 = not clear/does not address content).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scoring guidance used in study: 1–5 scale; both RCs and SCs addressed content but RCs did so more (coders’ medians RC=1, SC=2). Used to distinguish content-focused vs peripheral comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Positive vs Negative statement coding (direction of comment statements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Coding whether individual statements in a comment are positive (coded 1) or negative (coded -1) toward the manuscript; used as analytic variable and aggregated per comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this study each coding unit (typically one sentence) was assigned 1 (positive) or -1 (negative); most statements were negative (2,670 negative vs 457 positive). Regression models used counts of positive+negative or only negative statements to compare RCs vs SCs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access review / Pre-screening (scope/deficiency filter)
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial pre-selection (access review) criterion to avoid overload of the discussion forum with papers that are clearly deficient or out of scope; manuscripts must pass rapid pre-screening to be posted as discussion papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACP practice: editor performs access review (with optional advice from referees) to filter out clearly deﬁcient or out-of-scope submissions before public discussion. Serves as a procedural quality-control step prior to interactive public review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone and civility of comments (abusive content censorship)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether comments are abusive/personal attacks (which can be censored) versus constructive; civility is a criterion for publication of interactive comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACP policy: interactive comments are published without peer review and revision but can be censored in case of abusive commenting (personal offence, etc.). Study notes no need for editorial intervention in their dataset; civility matters for whether comments remain part of the public record.
